title: Machine-learning-guided peptide design yielded non-hemolytic anticancer candidates
summary: A recurrent neural network generated peptide sequences and classified predicted activity and hemolysis; a genetic-algorithm route also generated analogues. After sequence and physicochemical filters, researchers synthesized and tested 33 peptides. The paper reports 11 active anticancer peptides in its cell assays, four non-hemolytic under its red-cell assay. These in-vitro results do not establish cancer-cell specificity, clinical safety or therapeutic efficacy. A related 2020 modeling paper is separate from this experimental study; no claim of absolute sequence novelty is made.
ai_technology: Generative recurrent neural network, genetic algorithm, and recurrent-neural-network activity and hemolysis classifiers

source_review.scope: Primary publisher metadata and primary PubMed abstract/affiliation block; full PMC endpoint returned a browser verification challenge in this review.

evidence.tested: The abstract reports that 33 peptides were experimentally evaluated, 11 were active in anticancer cell assays, and four of the active peptides were non-hemolytic in the reported assays.
evidence.unknown: In-vitro activity and red-cell hemolysis do not establish cancer-cell specificity, clinical safety or treatment efficacy. Detailed potency measurements and absolute sequence novelty were not reassessed in this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: RNN and genetic-algorithm generation with RNN activity and hemolysis classifiers guided peptide selection for synthesis and testing.
